As thy hands, trembling with ancient anticipation, placed the purple-black helm upon thy crown, a most peculiar sensation befell thee — as if the very boundaries betwixt mortal flesh and the ethereal realms had grown thin. 'Twas akin to witnessing the great ice - floes of the Northern Wastes yield to spring's unstoppable advance, or to sailing the perilous currents of the Astral Plane aboard a vessel crafted of naught but ritual and will. A most curious chill descended upon thy fingertips, reaching deep unto bone and marrow, whilst within the helm's secretive confines, an entity not of mortal origin began to weave its psionic lattice of power and intent. What ancient might, what forgotten arts shall this eldritch discovery bestow upon its bearer? Verily, the answer lies in the whispers of destiny that now encircle thy thoughts.
Summon 22 loot chests with all Ancient Mega Pack items sorted by category. For testing and cheating only! Chests auto-delete when dropped.

A young shaman of the Stormcaller clan spent months observing tempests in the mountain pass, recording every flash, every strike — until lightning struck him directly, leaving only a melted medallion at the center of scorched earth. His companions found him three days later, wandering the slopes and muttering about "the dance between strikes." Inside the amulet still beats the storm he caught — that final one.

These ancient boots were crafted by Netherese wizards studying the limits of transmutation magic. Their creator willingly turned himself to stone, but his will continued to resonate through the rock, creating powerful vibrations capable of crushing enemies. Heavy metallic plates are built into the soles specifically to amplify this effect.
When you are Petrified, at the start of each of your turns in combat, your stone body creates powerful vibrations, dealing [1] to all foes within [2].
Powerful vibrations emanate from the petrified body, creating destructive sonic waves.

Magical runes envelop the metal of this slender one-handed hammer, covering almost its entire surface with a bright blue glow. When you touched the handle, you immediately jerked your hand away - it shocks! But after getting used to it, you even found it had a light massaging effect. Of all the runes you tried to decipher, you could only translate one word - Rrangundyr, whatever that means.

Every facet of this filigree sword gleams like gold, and the blade is honed to such perfection that one can even hear the light musical ringing of the blade in battle.

For a millennium, the Verdant Watch has stood vigil in the Chondathan Wood, where ancient tree-pollen forms an armour harder than mithral upon their sacred plates. Their eternal duty: to contain the Rotting Heart, that corrupted seed of the primordial forest which pulses with malevolent life in the deepwood's forbidden groves.

The death-priests of ancient Thay wove these vestments from the burial shrouds of a thousand martyrs who died in ecstasy, their souls willingly surrendered to the Bone Throne. Each thread pulses with thanaturgic essence — the concentrated joy of those who embraced oblivion as liberation. To wear it is to become a conduit between the living and the grateful dead.

If a foe successfully resists your necromancy spell, regain an Action Point.

When Archmage Khalandros breached the Far Realm seeking the Primordial Equation, reality itself recoiled from his hubris. His robes became a living paradox — threads woven from possibility itself, shifting through spectrums beyond mortal perception. Those who wear them report seeing colors that have no names, hearing the whispers of spells yet uncast.

In the shadow-draped halls of Castle Ravenloft, nine noble bloodlines willingly offered their scions to sanctify this vestment. Blind oracles wove moonless silk with threads drawn from willing veins, each stitch a prayer to the eternal night. The robe remembers its baptism — that cursed eve when mortality became a distant dream.
When dealing damage with Vampire Bite or Vampiric Touch, you additionally deal [1].

"Thus ended the glorious campaign against the treacherous Ghergs" — so the victors' histories record the extinction of an entire people. General Alierghast called them savages, barbarians, a threat to civilization. The truth died with them: they were farmers, poets, healers. Alierghast's own son knew this — he had secretly wed a Gherg woman, learning their gentle ways before war consumed everything. When she burned with her people, he spent twelve broken years trying to resurrect the dead. The ritual failed, but left this cursed mantle — woven from ashes and grief, holding fragments of the murdered innocent.
Call forth the spirit of a Gherg ancestor, seeking justice for their slaughtered people. The phantom weakens as it struggles to remain in the world that forgot them.
A mournful Gherg spirit appears beside the attacker, fighting your foes with the desperate fury of the extinct. Each turn weakens its fragile hold on existence.

If you are a human or half-elf (or disguised as one), gain +[1] Reaction Point.

You can spend a reaction when you or an ally are hit to summon a grieving Gherg spirit.

In the deepest forges of Mithral Hall, where rivers of molten adamantine flow like water, master smiths wrought this armour from meteoric iron blessed by Clangeddin himself. Each plate was tempered in dragonfire and quenched in the tears of stone giants. The Silverbeard clan presented it to their greatest champions — those who stood alone against the darkness and prevailed.
You gain permanent <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="MAG_BLADE_WARD">Blade Ward</LSTag>.

Vallen Despana earned no glory in Menzoberranzan's arena — she earned exile. A century of mercenary work yielded a hundred conquered foes, and from each she claimed a single plate of armour. In the forges of Skullport, she had them reforged into this impossible suit: each piece molecularly realigned to create armour that moves like shadowsilk yet deflects like adamantine. "Every plate," she would say, "is a life I took. Every life, a lesson learned."

If you are a drow (or disguised as one), gain +[1] Movement Speed, +[3] to Weapon Attack Rolls and +[2]% to Jump distance. Wearing this armour as a drow also grants immunity to Opportunity Attacks and [2]% reduction to fall damage.

"Case #847: Prisoner discovered dimensional glitch in Cell B-12. Subject began duplicating bread loaves exponentially. Upon breach: 14 tons of baked goods. Subject near death from starvation — no bread touched. Note: Robe's enchantment prevents removal once worn. Consider for repeat offenders." — Crumpled note from Waterdeep Prison archives.

Cursed Artifact.

The cosmic scales of justice tip against you — this cursed vestment binds to your very soul. Once donned, it cannot be removed by any mortal means. Consider it your scarlet letter, your mark of shame, your eternal "kick me" sign from the universe itself.

Before the gods walked Toril, before fire knew warmth, the First Winter descended. From its heart arose the Throne of Absolute Zero, and upon it sat the Nameless King — neither living nor undead, but something between. His plate mail was forged from meteoric ice that fell when stars still dreamed, each piece a fragment of cosmic winter given form.

Within the steel vessel, luminous essence swirls in patterns older than memory. The gear-toothed seal bears an artificer's mark — etched runes speaking of transmutation and binding, of power distilled from the very breath of dying stars. A faint warmth emanates through the tempered glass, as if something within yet dreams of the forge that birthed it.

Grimland was Twinsreach once. Heartland Folk and Coast Dwellers built it together, different but whole. Then came the Speaking Stones. Every voice heard at once. Every bitter word echoed back tenfold.

The Heartlands heard mockery. The Coasts heard hate. Truth drowned in the noise.

The Dividers got rich selling rage. Neighbors became enemies. Enemies became nothing. When the burning stopped, both sides had won. Both sides had lost.

This cloak comes from that nowhere place. They say it changes color depending who looks at it. They say a lot of things in Grimland. Nobody listens anymore.
While bearing any curse, you are enlarged.
You fool! You must realize you are doomed. The Harvester of the Dark One brooks no survivors...

Seraph Kaelith tore out her own wings to save a dying soldier — the last one standing after his entire legion fled. She fell for this act, but the armour born from her sacrifice lives on after millennia. To wear it is to drown in liquid starlight.

Aurelius killed seventeen children in the village of Greenvale. The celestial champion wept as his blade sought the demon hiding in each small body, missing again and again while divine fire consumed them anyway. The demon escaped. The gauntlets remember every name.

A cult believed that blinded people became more susceptible to the Weave's influence. Among their enchantments was this helm, its patterns refined over centuries with carefully inscribed arcane symbols. When complete, the high priest used it in the cult's most important ceremonies... until an acolyte murdered him out of simple envy. The thief hoped to wield the helm's power but didn't know the proper blinding rituals. The artifact, alas, drove him mad, and when sellswords found the gibbering fool on the roadside, they simply took the "metal thing" and sold it at the first goblin outpost along with the rest of their junk.
Your Necromancy spells reduce the number needed to score a Critical Hit by [1] against Blinded targets.

Many wondered what secret lay behind the famed bandanas of the Jolly Lads crew: each fighter wielded dirty tricks with uncanny skill in ship battles. The bandanas were soaked in a special compound containing snake scale oil, but the exact recipe remains unknown — and likely will stay that way, now that the entire gang perished along with half of Luskan during Brambleberry and Captain Deudermont's siege.
You gain +[1] to Spell Save DC while within [2] of a foe.

This worn and rust-spotted helm wasn't always so diminished: millennia ago it gleamed at coronation ceremonies in the lesser kingdoms before Netheril's rise. A relic of the Arkeng dynasty - those who settled matters of succession by ancient right. The hand-selected ash pheasant feathers appear recently added.
Using Righteous Clarity grants you Blessed for [1] turns.

The mask's red veins are Shadovar cinnabar, mined only in the depths beneath Anauroch by the Sunset Clan. This clan long served the Princes of Shade, but vanished during one of their experiments with the Shadow Weave. The mask was found in an abandoned sanctum centuries later, changing hands a dozen times before settling in a junk shop in Waterdeep.
While you are not illuminated, restore [1] Sorcery Point at the start of each turn in combat.
Restore [1] Sorcery Point at the start of each turn in combat.

This hat belonged to a mortal bard kept at Titania's court as an exotic curiosity. The feathers were strictly matched to the current season of the Feywild, earning the bard his nickname. When a portal between worlds accidentally opened during yet another performance, the Fashion Prince was literally pushed back to the Material Plane for an inappropriate verse and general annoyance. The hat remains the only proof of his century-long service to the fey.
When near a Charmed(or similar condition) foe in combat, you restore [1] Bardic Inspiration at the start of your turn.

This hood was sewn from purple wyvern leather and gifted to a wandering cartographer by an elven hermit from Evereska. For thirty years he mapped the forgotten paths of Anauroch, and she saw in his eyes the same weariness as in hers after centuries of life. "Your mind is sharper than your bow," she said, enchanting the leather, - "let one aid the other." This noble artifact, having lost none of its rich color over millennia, was found during archaeological excavations near Anauroch, alongside massive piles of decomposed maps.

An ordinary beekeeper from Triboar created a special mead that could intoxicate even dwarves with a single spoonful. The hat protected him from his own swarm until he confused it and put it on backwards. The enraged bees chased him through the entire town. The hat was retrieved from a tavern weathervane a week later and would have been forgotten if a passing wizard hadn't noticed the Weave's peculiar influence around the bright green band, which apparently had been soaked in that very special honey. The hat was sent to Candlekeep, where its enchantment was further enhanced and awarded to a forest ranger for loyal service to the wizards' interests.

Some trees grow with roots in earth and crown in sky. This one grew the opposite - roots in stars. The circlet was cut from such a tree at the hour when the Harp constellation stood above the Oak - once in seven hundred years. The blue within is not decoration, but windows. Through them, starlight enters and becomes earthly, while earthly wisdom rises to the heavens. The wearer hears the pulse of constellations in their own heartbeat.

When dealing[1], no more than once per turn restore a Bonus Action, but you must succeed on a Constitution Saving Throw([2]) or become Stunned for 1 turn. If you are concentrating, you skip this save.

The hat was found in the ruins of a bladesong school. Three times. A hundred years apart. Each time in the exact same place, as if just left there. The bright blue fabric never fades with time, as if renewed each time by someone invisible to mortal perception.
Attacks against foes with daggers, shortswords, longswords, rapiers, scimitars or sickles deal additional damage equal to your Intelligence Modifier × [1] - even on a miss.
Your levelled spells also deal [1] when your HP are less then half.
Your constructed form grants you Advantage on a Weapon Attack Rolls and Resistance to[1].

Worn by an Aquamancer of Umberlee, who read the ocean's moods and commanded its currents. He walked into the Great Tsunami to calm it, and was seen no more. These gloves were found a year later in a fisher's net, bone-dry, as if the sea remembered its master.

Woven from the fur of Auril-blessed bears for a priestess whose breath could freeze a man's blood. When her citadel fell, only this mantle remained upon a frost-rimed throne, a testament that winter's return is ever certain.

Forged of unmelting glacier-ice and silver runes, it guarded Auril's shrine for five centuries. It turns spells to ice shards, and its crystalline heart still pulses, waiting to turn arcane fury back upon its source.
Adamantine bracers inscribed with Helm's Vigilant Eye. Each demonic blow was met with divine radiance. Though their order fell, the gauntlets seek a new Warden to swear the Eternal Vigil.

A simple band of polished obsidian, saturated with conviction. Its bearer, Sir Marcus, wore it defending Elturel until the city fell. It now seeks a soul to bear an impossible promise: to protect the helpless, whatever the cost.

Dwarf-wrought, it sings a harmony between plate and shield, turning gear into a living fortress. Found amidst shattered weapons in a fallen hall, its runes yet glow for a warrior who understands strength in unity.

A silver shield bearing a shard of Mount Celestia. It purged the undead with sacred flame. Its last bearer fell to a lich, but the Aegis burned for three days, and the whispers of freed souls still echo within it.

Pale blue the substance of these exquisite slippers shimmers — now solid, now ghostly it shifts with each fleeting moment, surely ensorcelled. Their tips curl upward in the manner of true Calimite footwear, wrought by hands that knew the old ways. He who dons these stands in two places at once — seen and unseen, here and elsewhere.
Surrounded by silver mist, teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. After teleporting, gain Longstrider for 3 turns.
After using Ethereal Step, you gain Longstrider for 3 turns.

The soles are studded with chitinous hooks — eight there are not, nor yet ten, the count eludes the eye. Within lies a viscid film, as though a spider crawled there but moments past. A drow merchant in Menzoberranzan's markets swore upon her life: these slippers bore witness to an ancient curse. Spiders yearn to walk as men do, and men to crawl through darkness.
You cannot be enwebbed or slowed by it. Each turn in combat, you create webbing around yourself in a [1] radius.
All burning objects and creatures within [1] of you are instantly extinguished. Objects in this radius also begin emitting webbing.

Ragged the bindings, hastily stitched, so sodden with blood that no washing will cleanse them. Upon the soles a circle of prints — nine warriors there were who clasped their hands as one.

An oath is carved beneath in the elder tongue: "My fury flows into your veins. Not brothers are you to me by blood — but by deeds of war."
While you are raging, your successful attacks against foes heal all allies for [1]. Triggers once per turn.
While you are raging, your successful attacks against foes heal all allies for [1]. Triggers once per turn.

Soft they are, black as midnight's heart, sewn with thread that seems to melt in light. No tracks do these boots leave, as you have discovered. Fashioned to order, that much is clear from their elegance.
Sneak Attacks have a [1]% chance to grant you invisibility for [2] turn(s).

The velvet is worn at the heels, golden embroidery beginning to unravel. Seams form a wondrous pattern, symbolizing what appears to be the Weave's intricacies. A sorceress's daughter stitched these for her mother, who paced the halls of her Baldur's Gate estate through nights uncounted, walking storms into being that suffused these slippers with magic.
Regain [1] Sorcery Point(s) after each spell you cast in a turn after the first.
Spending Sorcery Points to cast spells grants you [1].

Bright yellow cloth you notice, untouched by time it seems, unlike the iron that threatens to crumble at any moment. First a healer wore them, fell holding the gates. Second a cleric wore them, fell shielding children. Third a sellsword wore them, fell buying time for the caravan. All this the boots remember, having drunk deep of these righteous warriors' life force, and now they grant their blessing when the wearer seeks to save companions.
When an ally within [1] of you enters the downed state, you gain Action Surge until the end of your turn.
Upon receiving Action Surge, you regain [1]% HP.

While under <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="ACTION_SURGE">Action Surge</LSTag>, you don't provoke <LSTag Tooltip="OpportunityAttack">Opportunity Attacks</LSTag> and your allies receive maximum possible healing.

A curious piece this, and passing strange in appearance. These boots were wrought for deep mining work, fitted with clever mechanisms of copper, steel, and specially enchanted white leather. The Thunder Peaks Mining Guild commissioned them after a cave-in, to detect dangerous resonances before stone yields. The mechanism worked too well. Wearers heard echoes of conversations not yet spoken, footsteps approaching through empty tunnels, the sound of picks striking stone that would be mined only hours hence. The Guild sold this uncanny artifact to enterprising goblins at the nearest market, eager to be rid of it.
You gain +[1] Reaction Point for [2] turn(s) after receiving Reverberation.
